slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.subtitle: By the end of this lecture, you will be able to:
key_points: Explain the Model–View–Controller pattern and why it separates concerns in modern web apps
Trace a request end-to-end through client events, Next.js route handlers, Drizzle ORM, and React views
Read and write TypeScript code that queries and mutates a relational database from a dedicated model layer
Run, extend, and debug a production-ready full-stack GIS tracker in VS Code with Bun & Next.js
slides.visual_description: Four horizontal dark cards with glowing teal-emerald circular numbered badges (1 to 4), clean white typography.

slides.title: What Is MVC?
slides.subtitle: A design pattern that splits an application into three interconnected parts, each with one job.
slides.key_idea: The Controller never writes SQL directly, and the View never contains database logic. Each layer can change without breaking the others.
slides.visual_description: Three interconnected nodes: MODEL (Emerald, Data & rules) <--> CONTROLLER (Cyan, Traffic cop) <--> VIEW (Blue, What you see) with directional flow arrows.

slides.title: Why Separate Concerns?

cards.title: Maintainability
cards.description: Fix bugs or redesign UI components without cascading unintended side-effects across other layers.

cards.title: Reusability & Multi-Storage
cards.description: The same Model layer powers the interactive map, admin dashboard, export CLI, and API consumers.

cards.title: Team Workflow
cards.description: Frontend engineers work on vector SVG gestures while backend engineers optimize relational schemas in parallel.

cards.title: Testability & Type Safety
cards.description: Strict TypeScript contracts (FullDistrict, Place, TrackerState) guarantee type safety across all boundaries.

slides.title: Request Lifecycle: Adding a Place
slides.subtitle: Follow one user request from the browser interface all the way to PostgreSQL and back.
steps: User submits 'Add Place' form in District Bottom Sheet [VIEW → POST /api/districts]
Next.js App Router routes request to the API controller [ROUTES → app/api/districts/route.ts]
Controller verifies JWT auth & validates payload input [CONTROLLER → isAuthenticatedAdmin()]
Model layer executes Drizzle ORM insert into PostgreSQL [MODEL → db.insert(places).values(...)]
Cache revalidated; SWR refetches; district glows emerald [CONTROLLER → SWR → VIEW]

slides.title: Summary & Discussion
bullets: Full-Stack MVC separates an application into Model (data), View (display), and Controller (flow & security).
The Controller is the single coordinator that manages validation, auth guards, and cache revalidation.
Relational databases enforce data integrity via schemas, foreign keys, and cascading relationships.
The same architectural principles scale from small tracker apps to enterprise geospatial platforms.
